title: The Apple, Please
can_do: 在两个可见选项中礼貌请求自己想要的物品，并在拿错时修正。
trigger: Mom offers two snack choices, then hands over the wrong one by mistake.
core_response: Can I have the apple, please?
stretch_response: Can I have the red apple, please?
repair_response: No, I mean the apple, please.
essential_props: one red apple and one banana

turns.speaker: mom
turns.line: You look hungry. Apple or banana?

turns.speaker: child
turns.line: Can I have the apple, please?

turns.speaker: child
turns.line: No, I mean the apple—the red one, please.

turns.speaker: mom
turns.line: Oh! I picked up the wrong one.

turns.speaker: mom
turns.line: Here's the apple you asked for.

replay_cards.title: Pack a picnic snack
replay_cards.setting: Packing a bag before going out
replay_cards.change: Mom offers a red apple or a green pear for the picnic
replay_cards.challenge: Child asks, 'Can I have the red apple, please?' If Mom reaches for the pear by mistake, Child says, 'No, I mean the apple, please.' Mom acknowledges the mix-up, puts the apple in his bag, and checks that his snack is ready.

replay_cards.title: Choose a book
replay_cards.change: Dad offers the bear book or the train book for tonight's story
replay_cards.challenge: Child asks for the bear book. If Dad picks up the train book by mistake, Child names the bear book again. Dad checks the cover with him, and they open the agreed book and begin reading.

parent_support: Offer two choices the child can see, then wait for his request.
If you pick up the wrong one, acknowledge the ordinary mistake as soon as he clarifies; do not prolong it to test him.
Accept a short correction or a useful visible detail. Use a normal voice and small gestures, then let him confirm the result and close politely.
